title: 2026届高三英语听力仿真训练（14）｜体育健身
note: 原创仿真训练，按 2026 高考听力题型编写（第一节、第二节均播放两遍）。

sections.name: 第一节
sections.desc: 听下面5段对话。每段对话后有一个小题，从题中所给的A、B、C三个选项中选出最佳选项。听完每段对话后，你都有10秒钟的时间来回答有关小题和阅读下一小题。每段对话读两遍。

materials.label: 第1段材料
materials.transcript:
M: How much is the gym for a month?
W: A hundred and fifty yuan for one month, or four hundred for three months.
M: I'll take the three-month card. It works out cheaper.
W: Good choice. Photos are taken upstairs.

questions.text: How much will the man pay for the card?

materials.label: 第2段材料
materials.transcript:
W: Will you run in the 800 metres at the sports meeting?
M: No, my knee still hurts. I'll do the long jump instead.
W: But you said you were bad at jumping.
M: I've been practising for two weeks.

questions.text: What event will the man take part in?

materials.label: 第3段材料
materials.transcript:
M: Is your ankle better?
W: Much better. The doctor said I could start training again, but only for twenty minutes a day at first.
M: So no long runs yet.
W: Not for another month. I'll wear a bandage for a while too.

questions.text: How long should the woman train each day at first?

materials.label: 第4段材料
materials.transcript:
W: I've started going to the gym at seven in the morning.
M: Really? I'd find that impossible. I can't move that early.
W: It's quiet then, and I feel fresh all day.
M: Maybe I should try. I keep falling asleep on the sofa after work.

questions.text: Why does the woman go to the gym early?

options.A: It is quiet and she feels fresh.
options.B: It is cheaper in the morning.
options.C: Her class is only held then.

materials.label: 第5段材料
materials.transcript:
M: Did you watch the final? Five sets and over two hours.
W: I fell asleep in the third set. Who won?
M: Lily. But Adam played better in the last two sets.
W: I always miss the best part.

questions.text: Who won the final?

sections.name: 第二节
sections.desc: 听下面5段对话或独白。每段对话或独白后有几个小题，从题中所给的A、B、C三个选项中选出最佳选项。听每段对话或独白前，你将有时间阅读各个小题，每小题5秒钟；听完后，各小题将给出5秒钟的作答时间。每段对话或独白读两遍。

materials.label: 第6段材料
materials.transcript:
W: Good morning. I'm interested in joining the gym.
M: Sure. May I ask what you're looking for? Weights, or something like dancing?
W: Mostly I want to get fitter. I sit all day at work.
M: Then you might like our morning class. It's forty minutes of stretching and light exercise, and it's popular with office workers.
W: How often does it meet?
M: Three times a week, on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. It's included in the membership.
W: And what does the membership cost?
M: Two hundred a month, or you can pay for a year and get one month free.
W: I'll start with one month, thank you. When can I begin?
M: As soon as you fill in this form. And bring a photo for your card.

questions.text: What do we know about the morning class?
Why does the woman want to join the gym?

materials.label: 第7段材料
materials.transcript:
M: Good morning, doctor. My shoulder hurts when I swim.
W: How long has it been like this?
M: About three weeks. I thought it would go away.
W: Do you swim every day?
M: Five days a week, for an hour.
W: That's probably the problem. Muscles get stronger when they rest.
M: So should I stop swimming?
W: No, but cut it to three times a week for a month, and make each session thirty minutes.
M: Can I do anything else?
W: Warm up for ten minutes before you get in the water, and put ice on the shoulder afterwards.
M: How long should I put the ice on?
W: Ten minutes at a time, no more.
M: Should I take medicine?
W: Only if the pain keeps you awake. Try the other things first.

questions.text: How often does the man swim now?
What does the doctor advise the man to do?
When does the doctor say to take medicine?

options.A: If the pain stops him sleeping.

materials.label: 第8段材料
materials.transcript:
W: Mr. Hall, how many students have signed up for the sports meeting?
M: Two hundred and ten, twenty more than last year.
W: Do we have enough helpers?
M: We need twenty, and last year we had only eighteen. It was hard.
W: I can ask the art class. They're good at making signs too.
M: That would help. Now, about the timetable. The first field event is at nine, but the grass may still be wet.
W: So keep the field events at nine?
M: Yes, and move the running races to ten.
W: Good. The parents will arrive around eleven for lunch.
M: Right. We should also remind them not to park on the road.
W: I'll put that in the letter we send home.
M: Good. And print a map for them too.

questions.text: How many students signed up last year?
Who will the woman ask to help?
When will the running races start?

materials.label: 第9段材料
materials.transcript:
M: I'm thinking of running the city marathon in April.
W: Have you run one before?
M: A half marathon, two years ago. It took me two hours and ten minutes.
W: That's not bad. But a full marathon is another matter. How many weeks do you have?
M: Eighteen. Is that enough?
W: Just about. Most plans take twenty weeks. You'll need to run four times a week, and the long run on Sunday should get longer each time.
M: How long should the longest run be before the race?
W: About thirty kilometres, three weeks before. Then you rest and eat well.
M: I'm worried about my knees.
W: Then don't increase the distance too fast. Ten per cent a week is the rule.
M: Should I join a club?
W: I would. Running alone is lonely, and people in clubs know the safe routes.
M: Good. My friend Ben is in one. I'll ask him on Thursday.

questions.text: How long did the man's half marathon take?
What does the woman say about the man's plan?

options.B: It is too late to start.

questions.text: What is the rule for increasing distance?
What does the woman think of joining a club?

materials.label: 第10段材料
materials.transcript: M: Before you start using the machines, let me say a few words about safety. First, always warm up for five to ten minutes, because cold muscles are easily hurt. Second, if something feels painful, stop at once. Pain is not a sign of progress. Third, put the weights back where you found them, so nobody trips. If you are not sure how a machine works, just ask one of us. We would rather answer a question than treat an injury. Our trainers are here from six in the morning until ten at night, and any of them can help you plan a programme. If you have not exercised for a long time, book a free check with the nurse first. Finally, please bring a towel and wear clean shoes. The changing rooms close fifteen minutes before the gym does.

questions.text: Where is the talk most probably given?
What does the speaker say about pain?
What must members bring?
